audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read [Skill, Sion, Sion, Skill, Skill, Sion, Sion]; the packet reads [Sion, Sion, Skill, Skill, K'Sante, Skill, Sion] and the mirrored ksante__sion audit is already on it.
audit.why: The page's own text supports the packet: whys[0] says he is weak at level 1 (Sion), whys[2] calls level 3 'genuinely even' (Skill), whys[4] hands level 6 to All Out (K'Sante). Only four tokens were wrong.
audit.corrected: Four rows flipped as matched full/content pairs: L1 Sion, L3 Skill, L6 K'Sante, 1st item Skill. L2, L4-5 and 2+ items already agreed.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] states All Out's cooldown as 90 seconds.
audit.why: The kit gives 120/100/80 — it is 120s at rank 1, a full 30 seconds longer than the page claims, and the whole 'trade in the gaps' plan is built on that number.
audit.corrected: 120s at rank 1 written into whys[5]; Path Maker's 14s rank-1 cooldown written into early and whys[3] so the dash-punish window is countable too.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page invents a percent-max-HP true damage passive for K'Sante and repeats it in seven fields ('percent-HP passive', 'his W-empowered autos deal true damage based on your max HP').
audit.why: Riot's passive text is 'K'Sante's Abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack. When All Out, K'Sante deals more damage with all Attacks and Abilities.' There is no percent-health and no true damage in it. The true damage in his kit belongs to Path Maker (W). This flipped the advice: the page told the player their HP stacking was the liability, when the real conclusion is that ARMOUR is the wasted stat and health is fine.
audit.corrected: Passive restated as an ability-mark that cashes in on his next attack. True damage attributed to Path Maker. Ntofo Strikes restated as a 450-range line on 3.5s that pulls at two stacks — it is not a knockup. Path Maker restated as a charge-up with damage reduction that knocks back and stuns, and stops stunning while All Out.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds anywhere despite All Out granting him healing.
audit.why: Brief flags needs-antiheal and Riot's R text says he 'gains increased damage, healing, and transformed abilities'. Sion's plan is a grind; unanswered healing undoes it.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal written into whys[4], mid and late, timed before you contest All Out.

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out's opening knockback is never described.
audit.why: Brief flags terrain-cuts-retreat: R 'knocks an enemy back, launching them through any wall in their path'. Sion has no dash, so being launched through a wall is a death sentence — Flash is for the wall, not for the damage.

edits.after: Use Path Maker's charge-up to soak your full-charge Q, then dash out of the combo that kills him

edits.before: Level 1 and 2, K'Sante is deceptively weak — his Q knockup costs him HP to charge too, and his passive damage requires sustained autos you can deny by walking away. Pop your W-shield the moment he steps in for an auto-trade and let the detonation chunk him while he cannot proc his passive more than once or twice. Level 3, his kit is online but your charged Q off a bush angle or post-E-shove hits him too slowly to dodge — land it and the stun pays for the whole sequence. His W-dash cooldown at early ranks is long; you get a clean window every 20-plus seconds.
edits.after: Level 1 and 2, K'Sante is deceptively weak — Ntofo Strikes is a 450-range line and his passive only pays off on the next attack after an ability, so step out of that follow-up and he gets nothing. Pop your W-shield the moment he steps in for an auto-trade and let the detonation chunk him. Level 3, his kit is online but your charged Q off a bush angle or post-E-shove hits him too slowly to dodge — land it and the stun pays for the whole sequence. Path Maker is 14s at rank 1, so every time he spends the dash you get a long clean window to charge.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are genuine skill-checks: K'Sante can W-dash through your charged Q if he reads the wind-up, and you have no meaningful spike yet to force a decisive trade. Farm safely, watch for him shoving to roam, and do not waste your E armor-shred on a K'Sante who has W available — he will dash out and you lose the trade tempo. At Level 6 his All Out becomes the dominant threat: it strips his resistances, makes him a duelist, and isolates you in a prolonged brawl where his percent-HP passive does real work. Respect it unless you are meaningfully ahead and can absorb the trade with your passive zombie threat.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are genuine skill-checks: K'Sante can Path Maker through your charged Q if he reads the wind-up, and you have no meaningful spike yet to force a decisive trade. Farm safely, watch for him shoving to roam, and do not waste your E armor-shred while his W is up — he dashes out and you lose the tempo. At Level 6 All Out becomes the dominant threat: it strips his resistances, gives him healing, and it opens by launching you back through any wall in the way — hold Flash for that wall, not for the damage. Buy Grievous Wounds before you contest the form, and respect it unless you are meaningfully ahead.

edits.before: Once Heartsteel is complete and your HP passive is compounding, every sustained brawl skews in your favor against a K'Sante who cannot proc his percent-HP passive fast enough through your W-shield cycles. Force fights when his W-dash is on cooldown — that removes his only reliable Q-dodge tool. At two-plus items, however, his passive true damage scales directly with your max HP and starts genuinely punishing your stack; trade briefly, reset with zombie pressure if you die, and lean on Unstoppable Onslaught to re-engage on your terms rather than sitting in his percent-HP window for extended brawls.
edits.after: Once Heartsteel is complete and your HP passive is compounding, sustained brawls skew your way against a K'Sante who has to land his marked follow-up attack through your W-shield cycles. Force fights while Path Maker is on cooldown — that takes away his Q-dodge and his stun at once. Watch the true damage on that same ability, though: armour buys you nothing against it, so keep stacking health and add Grievous Wounds rather than piling on resistances. Trade briefly, reset with zombie pressure if you die, and lean on Unstoppable Onslaught to re-engage on your terms.

notes: The dominant error was a fabricated ability: seven fields described a 'percent-HP passive' dealing true damage scaled to Sion's max health. Riot's Dauntless Instinct text has neither percent-health nor true damage — it marks a target so his next ATTACK hits harder. The true damage in K'Sante's kit sits on Path Maker. This inverted the itemisation logic the player would draw: the page implied HP stacking was self-defeating, when in fact armour is the stat that does nothing against the true-damage half of his kit. Also corrected: All Out is 120s at rank 1, not the 90s the page states; Ntofo Strikes pulls at two stacks rather than knocking up. Chart flipped on four matched pairs to the packet, matching the mirror. Full-layer strings carry mojibake em dashes; I made no full-layer prose edits here beyond the enum sides.
